entities.summary:
Francesco (Cicco) Simonetta was an Italian Renaissance statesman who composed an early treatise on cryptography.

Born in 1453, Simonetta served as a diplomat and strategist for various Italian city-states, including Milan and Florence.

In 1476, he was appointed as a member of the Council of Eight, a group of powerful politicians who advised the Duke of Milan.

Simonetta's treatise, which outlined methods for encrypting messages, was widely studied and used by European diplomats during the 16th century.

His legacy extends beyond cryptography, as he played a key role in shaping the political landscape of Italy during a time of great change and upheaval.

As he once said, 'The art of war is a science, not a game.' This quote encapsulates his pragmatic and strategic approach to politics.

Simonetta's significance lies in his ability to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries between Italian city-states, and his treatise on cryptography remains an important example of the intersection of politics and technology during the Renaissance.

Simonetta's diplomatic career was marked by several high-profile appointments, including his role as a member of the Council of Eight and his service as a diplomat to the French court.

Despite his many achievements, Simonetta's life was cut short in 1480, when he died under mysterious circumstances.
